defect_families.evidence: Authorization replay: the review identity is a SHA-256 over exactly its own claims, including the per-file operation and resulting blob and the fork point, so a review cannot be re-aimed at different content. The binding is deliberately to content rather than to a pull-request number, which is documented on verify_claims. Authenticated push evidence is bound to the exact SHA and the exact branch, so a run cannot be replayed onto another commit or another candidate.

Tamper and history forgery: a hand-edited review is detected by its own digest (test_a_hand_edited_review_is_detected_by_its_own_digest). Renaming a governed file onto an evidence-artifact path can no longer carry the source deletion out of the reviewed set; the exclusion is applied to expanded facts, and the push boundary and trusted admission both refuse a rename onto an evidence path.

Connector provenance and evidence lifecycle: the first draft of this gate would have handed the connector channel an unsatisfiable obligation, because the review artifact lies outside the connector's allowed paths -- a candidate carrying one would fail the path check and a candidate without one would fail the review gate. Repaired by excluding both governance-evidence artifacts from the receipt-bound content set while keeping the rename-destination constraint, and by exempting candidates that trigger no applicable family. Covered by test_the_review_artifact_is_governance_evidence_not_authorized_content and test_a_candidate_triggering_no_family_needs_no_review.

Writer identity: author and committer are resolved independently and exactly against the canonical binding; substring, prefix, suffix and domain lookalikes are refused, a bound name with an unbound email is not a partial match, mixed-writer ranges are refused, and missing or malformed policy, unreadable commit metadata and an unavailable fork point all fail closed. The canonically equivalent spelling is still admitted, so the guard does not block valid work.

Range evidence: the positive half (an authenticated push of the exact head on this exact branch by the bound writer) is mandatory, and the negative half (no ancestor may carry an authenticated push by another actor) preserves the security property the previous per-commit rule provided. A head push on another branch publishes nothing, and a malformed range SHA fails closed.

Receipt lifecycle: freshness is re-derived from git rather than believed, an exact receipt is not forced into unnecessary churn, an unparseable receipt fails closed, and the evidence-path scope matches what trusted admission re-derives. Repaired during this pass: applicability is derived from the change set, so a receipt inherited from the base branch is base state rather than a claim about a later candidate and removing one is a retirement; a receipt an ordinary branch actually writes is still refused, and a connector-namespace candidate that removes its own is still refused for carrying none. The stale Issue #407 receipt is retired at this head.

Ready gating: base, change set, applicable families and the governing Issue's acceptance criteria are all re-derived from trusted evidence, so a review can neither describe content that does not exist, nor narrow its own applicability, nor measure itself against criteria it wrote for itself. Unavailable review, family-catalog and Issue evidence all fail closed. Non-blocking findings deliberately do not block, so the gate cannot be satisfied by driving comment count to zero. Repaired during independent review (CDX-413-001): the criteria leg was self-attested and is now bound to the owner-authored Issue.

Pending versus failure: only the running state is transient; missing, invalid, untrusted-publisher and wrongly-bound proofs all remain failure. Repaired during independent review (CDX-413-002): a pending head is now reconciled by the candidate-admission controller when the trusted proof lands, so pending cannot become a way to stay Ready while unadmitted.

Overclaimed prevention: every family in this catalog is validated against the evidence it declares, and the PR #411 families are recorded at regression-tested rather than relabelled as prevented. The guard itself is exercised by paired positive and negative fixtures.

findings.evidence: The pre-ready review artifact is outside the connector ingress allowed paths, so binding it as receipt-authorized content would have made every connector candidate inadmissible either with or without a review. Resolved by treating both governance-evidence artifacts as evidence rather than content, keeping the rename-destination constraint on both.

Requiring a hostile review of every candidate would have permanently blocked dependency-only candidates, whose authors cannot produce the artifact. Resolved by requiring the review only when at least one recurring-defect family applies, while still verifying any review that is present.

Rename detection is a heuristic that local git and GitHub need not agree on, so a representation-dependent binding would have marked valid reviews stale. Resolved by expanding renames into removal plus addition on both sides.

Applying artifact exclusion to whole rename records would have let a rename onto an artifact path carry the source deletion out of the reviewed change set. Resolved by applying exclusion to the expanded facts, and by refusing renames onto evidence paths at the push boundary.
git diff --raw abbreviates blob SHAs, which are not comparable with the full digests GitHub reports and fail canonical normalisation outright. Resolved with --abbrev=40 and pinned by a regression.

Rejecting a review that names a family unknown to the trusted catalog would have blocked precisely the candidate that adds a family. Resolved by requiring coverage derived from the trusted catalog while tolerating extra names, which cannot make an incomplete review look complete.

A stale local base branch could have widened the governed commit range over already-merged history and blocked a valid push. Resolved by consulting only the remote-tracking base ref and failing closed with an actionable fetch instruction.

GitHub reports a source path for a copied file, which canonicalises to an addition; an addition carrying a source is rejected as malformed, so an ordinary copy would have blocked admission. Resolved by dropping previous_path for every non-rename status.

Found by this candidate's own push boundary refusing its first push. Since PR #411 merged the Issue #407 connector receipt onto the default branch, every later candidate inherits that file at its head. Both the new local receipt-freshness check and the pre-existing trusted connector re-derivation read mere presence as a claim about the current range, so an already-merged receipt spoke for unrelated work: every ordinary candidate was refused for 'carrying a connector authorization receipt outside the connector namespace'. This was a live blocking defect on main, not only in the new code. Resolved on both boundaries with one rule -- a receipt is this candidate's claim only when this candidate writes it, derived from the change set rather than from file presence. The relaxation is confined to the ordinary path: a connector-namespace candidate is unchanged, because every claim in its receipt is already re-derived against this exact range, branch, fork point and grant. An ordinary branch that actually writes a receipt is still refused. DFF-012 was widened to carry this invariant.

Confirmed on the hosted boundary: Hunter Governance Review published 'Candidate admission blocked: branch issue-412-pre-ready-hostile-review-gate-... carries a connector authorization receipt but is outside the connector namespace' for this exact head. The trusted controller runs the default-branch code, so the AUD-412-012 fix cannot apply to its own pull request -- the documented bootstrap property of this repository. The stale artifact itself therefore has to be retired at this head. The Issue #407 receipt on the default branch is bound to a deleted connector/issue-407-* branch and an older fork point, so it can never again be a valid claim for any candidate; the path is per-candidate evidence the connector authorizer overwrites, not an append-only audit record, and git history preserves it. Removing it clears the live block for every candidate, and Issue #412 states directly that stale Issue #407 receipt claims must never be carried into #412. The push boundary was corrected in the same batch so that retiring an inherited receipt is a retirement rather than a claim; a connector-namespace candidate that removes its own receipt is still refused by trusted admission, which requires a namespace candidate to carry one.

The review binds content rather than a pull-request number, so two candidates with a byte-identical diff from the same fork point share a review. This is intentional -- a review is a statement about a diff -- and is now documented on verify_claims rather than left implicit.

A guard_reference is validated structurally (the file exists and the symbol resolves), not semantically: a family could name a real but unrelated guard. Strengthening this would require a semantic link the repository does not currently model. Recorded rather than implemented; it does not make any contribution unsafe.

Identity comparison case-folds the email local part, which is technically case-sensitive in RFC 5321 although effectively case-insensitive at every relevant provider. Widening rather than narrowing risk is bounded to the two bound identities; recorded for visibility.

Independent review (Codex, P1) on scripts/hunter_pre_ready_review.py: the acceptance-criteria leg of the gate accepted any non-empty candidate-authored list as complete so long as one entry read 'satisfied'. Neither the claimed Issue nor the criterion text was compared with a trusted definition, so a review omitting all but one criterion, or naming one invented criterion, was structurally complete and could admit the candidate. Verified and accurate. Resolved by re-deriving the criteria from the owner-authored governing Issue via the GitHub API in the trusted controller, scoped to the Issue's own 'Acceptance criteria' section, and requiring every derived criterion to be covered; the Issue a review names must also be the Issue its branch binds. Extra entries stay allowed and unavailable Issue evidence fails closed.

Independent review (Codex, P1) on scripts/hunter_governance_review_v2.py: a head marked Ready while the trusted upgrade proof is still running is admitted as pending, and the Draft controller deliberately leaves a pending head alone -- but .github/workflows/hunter-candidate-admission.yml only reconciled on Hunter / Pre-PR Preflight completion, while trusted-upgrade completion triggered the status-only Governance Review. The head could therefore stay Ready indefinitely while unadmitted, contrary to unadmitted_head_state=draft. Verified and accurate, and the window predates this contribution for protected-preflight candidates while this contribution widens it. Resolved by subscribing the candidate-admission controller to Hunter / Trusted Preflight Upgrade completion and widening its event condition to accept a pull_request_target-originated workflow_run, rather than by turning pending back into a failure.

Found while writing the regression for CDX-413-001: the acceptance-criteria parser folded an indented sub-bullet into the text of the criterion above it, so a criterion carrying supporting detail could never be matched by a review that quoted the criterion itself -- a false-positive Ready block. Resolved by treating an indented bullet as sub-detail rather than as a continuation line, pinned by test_indented_sub_bullets_are_detail_not_criteria.
